info.title: Campbooks API
info.description: The Campbooks HTTP API. Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`. Operations require an OAuth 2.1 bearer token with the scope they list (401 without a valid token, 403 without the scope) unless they are public. The `/bff/*` operations serve the web app only: they authenticate with its session cookie instead of a token.

get.description:
A Server-Sent Events stream of what changed in the workspace, for clients
that keep a cache: each `change` frame names a record and an operation
(`{"cursor","record":{"type","id"},"op":"upsert"|"delete","version"}`),
never its contents; refetch what you show. Frames: `ready` (where the
stream starts), `change`, `heartbeat` (an SSE comment, or the cursor when
it moved past changes you may not see), `reset` (your cursor is unknown,
expired or too far behind: refetch everything, continue from the
cursor given), `revoked` (you no longer belong to the workspace) and
`closing` (the stream ends; reconnect with your cursor). Every frame
that carries a cursor sets the SSE `id`, so `EventSource` resumes on its
own. You only receive changes of records a read operation you hold a
scope for returns.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The last cursor received; resumes after it.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The last cursor received, for clients that cannot send
`Last-Event-ID` (the header wins when both are present). Omit it to
start from now.

get.summary: Read from the admin API as the signed-in administrator.
get.description:
`/bff/admin/<path>` is `/admin/<path>` (the admin API, ADR 0015) with
 the session's access token attached, exactly like `/bff/api/*`. Its
 answers are the admin API's own: 404 for anyone who is not an
 administrator with the operation's permission, 401
 `admin_reauth_required` when the last sign-in is more than 1 hour
 old (sign in again at `/bff/login?max_age=0`). Without a live session
 the answer is 401 `session_required`. POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE
 need the `X-Campbooks-CSRF: 1` header from the app's origin.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The admin API path after `/admin/`, e.g. `v1/system/overview`; may contain slashes.

200.description: The admin API's response, whatever its status.

503.description: `bff_not_configured`, or the identity provider is unavailable while the access token needs refreshing.

get.summary: Read from the API as the signed-in user.
get.description:
`/bff/api/<path>` is `/api/<path>` (same method, query, headers and

 it is about to expire. The token never leaves the server. Answers are
 the API's own; without a live session the answer is 401
 `session_required` (sign in at `/bff/login`). POST, PUT, PATCH and
 DELETE need the `X-Campbooks-CSRF: 1` header from the app's origin.

ids), to tell which mailbox a way in came with.

email.description:
The address the provider gave when it was added (shown, never used
to find an account).

last_used_at.description: When it was last used to sign in.

mailboxes.description:
For a way in a connect created: how many workspaces its mailbox is
connected in. It goes when the last of them is disconnected (unless
it is the last way in). 0 for any other way in.

mailbox_providers.description:
The providers a mailbox can be connected from (`identity.start_link`
with `connect`): offered, and with a mail adapter. Same order.

providers.description: The providers this instance offers, in display order.

WorkspaceClient.description: A workspace client, as settings show it. Never its secret.

last_used_at.description: When it last got a token.

scopes.description: The scopes it may ask for.

purge_after.description: When its records will be purged for good.

WorkspaceList.description: The caller's workspaces, oldest first, each with their role.

WorkspaceView.description: A workspace, as its members see it.

oneOf.description: The caller's role in it; absent for a client token.

bearer.description:
An OAuth 2.1 access token (a JWT) issued by this instance's identity provider, the issuer configured as `CAMPBOOKS_AUTH__ISSUER`. Each operation lists the scope it requires; operations with an empty requirement are public. Scopes:

- `admin:access`: Reach the instance administration API, if your account has an admin profile. Granted to Campbooks' own apps only.
- `attention:read`: See what needs you: the items on your Home.
- `attention:write`: Put items on your Home off until later, and bring them back.
- `connectors:read`: See the outside accounts connected to your workspaces and how their sync is doing.
- `connectors:write`: Connect outside accounts (such as Gmail), sync them now and disconnect them.
- `conversations:read`: Read your inboxes, conversations and messages.
- `conversations:send`: Write drafts and send messages, replies and forwards from your inboxes.
- `conversations:write`: Mark conversations read or unread, star, archive, label and move them between streams.
- `identity:clients`: Register, rotate and remove a workspace's own apps and their secrets.
- `identity:read`: See your account, its ways in and the mailboxes waiting to be connected.
- `identity:write`: Change your account and connect or discard the mailboxes waiting on it.
- `search:read`: Search the records you may read (conversations need conversations:read too).
- `system:read`: Read operational status.
- `workspaces:admin`: Manage workspaces you own or administer: settings, members, invitations, deletion and the security log.
- `workspaces:read`: See your workspaces and who belongs to them.
- `workspaces:write`: Create workspaces, accept invitations and leave workspaces.

session.name: __Host-campbooks_session
session.description: The web app's session cookie, set by `/bff/callback` (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict`; named `campbooks_session` when the instance's public URL is plain http). Unsafe methods also need the `X-Campbooks-CSRF: 1` header and a same-origin request.

tags.name: workspaces
tags.description: Workspaces, members and roles, invitations and the security log. Workspace-owned resources live under `/api/v1/w/{workspace_id}/`; a caller who is not a member (or a client token bound to another workspace) gets 404.

tags.name: connectors
tags.description: Connections to outside accounts (Gmail, Zoho Mail): connect with the provider's consent, see their health, sync now, disconnect. Credentials are never returned.

tags.name: conversations
tags.description: Inboxes, conversations and messages on any channel (email first), sorted into streams. Workspace-owned: a user sees the inboxes they are a member of; a client token bound to the workspace sees them all.

tags.name: identity
tags.description: Accounts and their ways in, and this instance's OAuth 2.1 authorization server: discovery, keys, authorization, tokens, revocation, sign-in with a provider, and the mailboxes a sign-up granted, waiting for a workspace. The protocol endpoints (`/.well-known/*`, `/oauth2/*`, `/auth/*`) serve browsers and OAuth clients; they answer 404 while another identity provider serves the instance.

tags.name: attention
tags.description: What needs you: one queue per member of what the records you may open ask of you (conversations today), with Later per member.

tags.name: search
tags.description: One search over the records you may open: conversations today. Words in English, Portuguese, Spanish and French with accents ignored, Gmail-style operators, highlights as plain-text segments. Results come only from the containers (inboxes) you may see, checked at query time.

tags.name: changes
tags.description: The change feed: a Server-Sent Events stream per workspace of the records that changed (ids only), so clients refetch only what they show.

tags.name: bff
tags.description: The web app's backend-for-frontend: sign-in, the session cookie and same-origin API access. Browsers only; other clients call `/api/*` with their own OAuth token.
